basis: Defining rib/thoracic abnormalities and developmental disability; restrictive respiratory insufficiency from thoracic hypoplasia affects most patients.
Bacterial infection of upper airways and oral mucosa with pseudomembranes; toxin-mediated myocarditis and neuropathy are minority complications.
Autosomal recessive nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss.
Proximal 18q deletion typically causes developmental delay and intellectual disability; no additional organ has sufficiently established common damage here.
Temple syndrome features motor/developmental delay, precocious puberty and obesity; joint hypermobility occurs in 12/19 patients. Scoliosis is below 30%.
Experimental transplantable mouse mammary carcinoma, not a human disease; its breast origin has no mapped axis.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting limb segments, vertebrae and joints; intelligence is normal.
Carcinoma defined by neoplastic infiltration of the skin.
Embryonal malignancy arising in the cerebellum.
Endocrine pancreatic insulin excess; elevated insulin alone does not establish hypoglycemic brain injury.
Developmental disability and congenital cardiac defects characterize the syndrome; cardiac anomalies in 2/6. Minor dysmorphism and tumor predisposition do not add axes.
SNCA-associated neurodegenerative parkinsonism; motor disability and autonomic symptoms reflect nervous system disease.
Lysosomal storage encephalopathy; hepatic and splenic storage with enlargement in 2/2 cases. Respiratory insufficiency is largely neurologic; optic atrophy is under 30%.
Carcinoma arising in paranasal sinuses, which belong to the airway axis; metastatic risk does not establish another involved organ.
Heart and chest/skeletal defects define NS; platelet dysfunction and developmental delay each occur in 30-79%. Eye morphology and hepatomegaly alone do not establish functional damage.
Spinal hemicord damage causes ipsilateral motor and contralateral sensory deficits; underlying causes do not define additional axes.
Brachydactyly and symphalangism with characteristic spinal and foot deformities.
Congenital endocrine islet dysfunction causes hypoglycemia; persistent hypoglycemic neurodevelopmental injury affects roughly 30-50% of congenital cases.
Congenital talonavicular dislocation and fixed foot deformity; definition specifies isolated disease, so associated neurologic syndromes are excluded.
Traumatic injury to nervous system structures; ocular injuries are particular subtypes rather than involvement across the umbrella.
Inherited quantitative fibrinogen deficiency is a coagulation disorder; mucosal bleeding does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal or airway damage.
Inherited degeneration of motor pathways causes progressive spastic paraplegia; additional organs vary among complicated subtypes.
Rabies virus directly causes fatal encephalomyelitis; salivation, gastrointestinal symptoms and vocal cord paresis do not establish separate organ damage.
Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma originating in the bladder, included in the renal axis.
Described syndrome combines gonadal/metabolic dysfunction, cardiomyopathy, blindness and deafness; hearing loss is a defining feature, satisfying the diagnostic-criterion exception.
